Subject: Post-demo: cost comparison and next tests

Tessa —

Thanks for the demo this morning. KineticApps liked the latency and the cache demos; a few follow-ups from our finance and infra teams:

- Can you provide a per-1M token cost comparison (Redwood vs Hyperscaler A vs Hyperscaler B) for a few model classes (open Llama-style, LLM-2-style) under our expected usage profile?
- We need unit economics that account for batching (batch sizes 1 / 8 / 32) and cache hit rates (0%, 50%, 90%) — our traffic has a ~40% reuse rate in practice but we'd like to see the sensitivity.
- Please include any hidden or amortized costs (e.g., long-lived KV caches, storage for pinned cache keys, pre/post-processing).

I've attached a zip with 20 sample prompts and a short example payload (kinetic-sample-prompts.json). If you can propose a concrete test matrix and expected timeline, we'll sign off on a small paid benchmark engagement.

Can you also confirm whether you can run the tests in our us-west region and whether you can normalize tokenization across vendors?

Appreciate it — Matt

Matt — thanks for the clear ask and the sample prompts. Internal notes below and a proposed plan attached (redwood-econ-plan.xlsx).

Quick answers:
- Yes, we can run tests from our us-west capacity and we'll normalize tokenization (we use the same tokenizer pipeline across vendors for fair comparison).
- We will produce per-1M token unit costs for each vendor/model pairing and show delta sheets that include amortized cache/storage overhead.

Proposed test matrix (high level):
- Models: Open-variant (quantized), LLM-2-class (fp16) — 3 model variants total (fast/standard/quality).
- Workloads: 3 batching configurations (1, 8, 32) x 3 cache hit scenarios (0%, 50%, 90%).
- Run size: target ~200k tokens per cell to reduce variance; aggregate and report normalized per-1M tokens.
- Metrics: cost per 1M tokens (raw), latency P50/P95, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and effective cost after cache hits.

Requests for internal owners: Ben — can you stand up the runs on dedicated infra and attach the runbook? Vivek — please include notes about quantization/throughput differences and where hyperscalers diverge (e.g., kernel availability, pre-compiled ops). Rishi — we may need a short pricing approval for a charged benchmark; will you confirm budget?

Next steps:
- Ben: deliver runbook and schedule capacity (ETA 24h).
- Redwood: run the 9 core cells and produce a delta summary (ETA 72h after runs start).
- Matt: provide sign-off on the paid benchmark engagement and confirm any additional telemetry you want captured.

Attaching: redwood-econ-plan.xlsx (high-level plan), demo-recording.mp4 (for reference).

Thanks — Tessa

Heads-up on things to normalize for fair hyperscaler comparisons:

- Preemptible/spot pricing: some hyperscalers advertise lower raw GPU/hour but with preemption — we should include both on-demand and spot buckets in the delta sheet and show variance.
- Batch efficiency: when we compare batching (1/8/32), ensure sequence-length distribution is identical — longer sequences can negate batch advantages. Use the canonicalized prompts for this.
- KV cache amortization: if we pin a large KV cache for 90% hit scenario, account for memory reservation costs and storage (persisted checkpoint) across the run window.
- Network/egress: hyperscalers sometimes bundle inference with remote storage; normalize network egress to the same region and document assumptions.

I'll add short notes in the runbook (test-runbook.md) about what kernels we expect to be missing on some runtimes and how to fall back. Also: include a short script that tokenizes consistently and stores the canonical tokens alongside logs.

Vivek
Principal Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference
